questions.q: What is a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)?
options: A manually maintained spreadsheet of approved vendors
A generated inventory of every component in a software build, including transitive dependencies
A list of security incidents from the past year
A pricing document for third-party licenses
questions.explain: An SBOM is an automatically generated inventory listing every component — direct and transitive — in a given software build, typically produced at CI time.

questions.q: What are the two standard SBOM formats mentioned in the lesson?
options: YAML and TOML
SPDX and CycloneDX
CVE and CVSS
SARIF and JUnit
questions.explain: SPDX and CycloneDX are the two dominant, widely-adopted standard formats for representing an SBOM.

questions.q: In a CycloneDX document, what does a component's "purl" field provide?
options: The component's CVSS severity score
A standardized package URL that uniquely identifies the component across ecosystems
The name of the developer who wrote the component
A timestamp of when the component was last updated
questions.explain: A purl (package URL) is a standardized identifier format that uniquely names a package regardless of which package ecosystem it comes from.

questions.q: Why does having SBOMs already generated matter most right after a new critical CVE is disclosed?
options: Because SBOMs automatically patch the vulnerability
Because teams can query existing SBOMs for the affected package in minutes instead of manually searching every repository
Because SBOMs are only valid for 24 hours after generation
Because new CVEs can only affect software that has an SBOM
questions.explain: With SBOMs already generated for every service, answering "are we affected" becomes a quick query instead of a manual, error-prone search across every repository's manifests.

questions.q: What does supply chain risk cover beyond "does a dependency have a known CVE"?
options: Nothing — supply chain risk is exactly synonymous with dependency CVEs
Whether the build pipeline itself was compromised and whether an artifact's provenance can be verified
Only the cost of licensing third-party software
Only the speed of the CI pipeline
questions.explain: Supply chain risk also includes whether a package came from a legitimate source and whether the build process itself can be trusted — addressed by frameworks like SLSA and tools like Sigstore/cosign, which verify provenance and signatures.
